lessons.title: Loop with range
lessons.description: Finish `sum_squares(n)`. Add up `1*1 + 2*2 + ... + n*n` using a loop or `range`. `sum_squares(3)` equals `14`. The test checks that `sum_squares(3)` equals `1 + 4 + 9`.
learning_objectives: range stops before its end, so range(1, 4) visits 1, 2, and 3.

source.name: Python official documentation (docs.python.org) — 4.2. for Statements — Conditional Control (range())

lessons.title: Practice List Comprehensions enumerate
lessons.description: Finish double_evens(numbers). Return a new list of each even number multiplied by 2. Skip the odd numbers. A list comprehension fits. double_evens([1, 2, 3, 4]) equals [4, 8]. The test checks that double_evens([1, 2, 3, 4]) equals [4, 8].
learning_objectives: This step adds each slot number and its reading, using items and 4.
lessons.solution_code:
def double_evens(numbers):
    return [x * 2 for x in numbers if x % 2 == 0]

source.name: Python official documentation (docs.python.org) — 5.1.3. List Comprehensions — Data Structures

lessons.title: Practice Discount Price Applier
lessons.description: Finish apply_discounts. Apply a percentage discount to all prices in a list using a comprehension: each price is reduced by discount_pct percent. The test checks that apply_discounts([100, 50], 10) equals [90.0, 45.0].
learning_objectives: This step subtracts two from each price and adds the results, using prices and 2.
lessons.solution_code:
def apply_discounts(prices, discount_pct):
    return [p * (1 - discount_pct / 100) for p in prices]

source.name: Python official documentation (docs.python.org) — 5.1.3. List Comprehensions — Data Structures

lessons.title: Practice Unit 10 Checkpoint Loops Mastery
lessons.description: filter_long_words(words, min_len) must return, via a list comprehension, only the words whose length is at least min_len. The test checks that filter_long_words(["hi", "hello", "hey"], 3) equals ["hello", "hey"].
learning_objectives: Using keep and 10, this step adds only the readings above the cutoff.
lessons.solution_code:
def filter_long_words(words, min_len):
    return [w for w in words if len(w) >= min_len]

source.name: Python official documentation (docs.python.org) — 5.1.3. List Comprehensions — Data Structures
